statement: Put $Q=F/F''$ and $R=\mathbb Z[Q]$. There is an exact sequence of discrete groups and an exact sequence of left $R$-modules \[ 1\longrightarrow F''/F'''\longrightarrow F/F''' \longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1, \qquad 0\longrightarrow F''/F'''\longrightarrow R^2 \xrightarrow{d}R\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathbb Z\longrightarrow0, \] where $d(a,b)=a(\bar x-1)+b(\bar y-1)$, with right factors in this formula and the regular left action on each term. This is an explicit module description over the noncommutative ring $R$.

statement: Let $L=\mathbb L_{\mathbb Q}(x,y)$, graded by total degree, and let $D^rL$ be the span of Lie monomials with at least $r$ occurrences of $y$. Put $v_i=\operatorname{ad}_x^i(y)$ and $V=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}\mathbb Qv_i$. There is an isomorphism of graded Lie algebras \[ L/D^3L\simeq \mathbb Qx\ltimes(V\oplus\Lambda^2V). \] Here $[v_i,v_j]=v_i\wedge v_j$, the bracket of $V$ with $\Lambda^2V$ vanishes, and $[x,v_i]=v_{i+1}$; the action of $x$ on $\Lambda^2V$ is the induced derivation. In weight $n\geq2$ the depth-two dimension is $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$. The identity on $x,y$ induces the surjection $L/L'''\twoheadrightarrow L/D^3L$ with kernel $D^3L/L'''$.

statement: Normalize the depth-one generators by $\bar\sigma_{2m+1}=\operatorname{ad}_x^{2m}(y)$. For the positive-weight Lie algebra of the outer pro-$\ell$ Galois image, tensored with $\mathbb Q_\ell$, the depth-one dimensions are one in weights $3,5,7,9,11,13$ and zero in the other weights at most fourteen. Its depth-two dimensions in weights $1,\ldots,14$ are \[ 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1,0,1,0,1,0,2. \] The first relation among the depth-one brackets is \[ \{\bar\sigma_3,\bar\sigma_9\} -3\{\bar\sigma_5,\bar\sigma_7\}=0 \quad\text{in depth two}. \] This is a statement after tensoring with $\mathbb Q_\ell$ and taking the specified filtrations; it asserts no integral saturation index.

statement: Let $q:F\twoheadrightarrow G$ be any finite quotient, $N=\ker q$, and $V(H)$ one of $H'$, $H''$, or $\gamma_{c+1}H$. There is a natural short exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow\frac{N\cap V(F)}{V(N)} \longrightarrow\frac{N}{V(N)} \longrightarrow \ker\left(\frac{F}{V(F)}\longrightarrow\frac{G}{V(G)}\right) \longrightarrow1. \] The comparison requested with target $G$ itself is the specialization $V(G)=1$ of this exact sequence. The map $F/V(F)\to G$ with composite $q$ exists exactly when $V(G)=1$.

statement: For every finite quotient $F\twoheadrightarrow G$ of order $d>1$, each of the three comparison kernels in E.6 is nonzero. For abelianization it is a free abelian group of rank $d-1$; the image is a rank-two lattice of index $|G^{\mathrm{ab}}|$ in $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$. For the nilpotent quotient of class $c$ its rational Hirsch rank is \[ \sum_{j=1}^c\bigl(w_j(d+1)-w_j(2)\bigr),\qquad w_j(r)=\frac1j\sum_{e\mid j}\mu(e)r^{j/e}. \]

statement: Write $G^{(p)}$ for the maximal $p$-group quotient of the finite group $G$. There is a continuous surjection \[ \widehat N_p\longrightarrow \ker(\widehat F_p\longrightarrow G^{(p)}). \] Its source is free pro-$p$ of rank $|G|+1$ and its target is free pro-$p$ of rank $|G^{(p)}|+1$. It is an isomorphism exactly for $p$-groups $G$. For $p$-groups the target is the open subgroup corresponding to the given cover. More explicitly, put $r=|G|+1$ and $s=|G^{(p)}|+1$. There are free pro-$p$ bases $a_1,\ldots,a_s,b_1,\ldots,b_{r-s}$ in the source and $\bar a_1,\ldots,\bar a_s$ in the target for which the comparison sends $a_i\mapsto\bar a_i$ and $b_j\mapsto1$. Its kernel is exactly the closed normal subgroup generated by those $r-s$ elements $b_j$. This description is noncanonical; the original continuous comparison is canonical.

statement: For $|G|=d$, the canonical morphism of rational prounipotent groups $N^{\mathrm{un}}\to F^{\mathrm{un}}$ is surjective. Its map on abelianized Lie algebras is a surjection $\mathbb Q^{d+1}\to\mathbb Q^2$ with kernel of dimension $d-1$. It is an isomorphism exactly for $d=1$. In suitable noncanonical free pronilpotent coordinates, its Lie algebra map sends $X,Y$ to the two target generators and $z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1}$ to zero. Its kernel is the closed ideal generated by the $z_j$; by free-Lie elimination it is the completed free Lie algebra on $\mathbb Q\langle X,Y\rangle\otimes \langle z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1}\rangle$, where a word acts by iterated adjoints. Exponentiation is the exact kernel group. Every morphism from a connected unipotent rational algebraic group to the constant finite group $G$ is trivial; thus the specified map to $G$ in a kernel formula descends only for the trivial quotient. The preceding surjection is the comparison obtained from the trivial completion of $G$.
